newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul bourse seen rising, securities shrs to lead.
newsitem.headline: Seoul bourse seen rising, securities shrs to lead.

text.p: South Korean stocks are forecast to continue rallying on Wednesday, driven by the Japanese yen's strength and the stable local money market, brokers said.
They saw securities shares leading the rally on hopes that their earnings would be boosted by the recent interest rate falls and the stock market's rise.
Buying will also be focused on large-capitalised, but cheap manufacturing stocks that have been relatively undervalued.
On Tuesday the composite index rose 1.87 percent, or 13.47 points, to a six-month closing high of 734.67.
The Japanese yen rose as high as 111.98 to the U.S. dollar on Tuesday in Tokyo.
"Although some correctional fluctuations are seen, an upward trend will continue," said Park Joo-chang of Daewoo Securities.
Brokers said securities houses, which heavily rely on short-term call money for funds, will benefit from the recent drops in the call rates based on a stable liquidity situation.
Overnight call rates are now at about 12.30 percent, down from about 13.00 percent last week.
